card.title: Why a link can fool you

panels.text: A link can look like it goes to example.com. But example.com.scam.com belongs to scam.com, despite appearing to refer to example.com.
Another tactic is to make the link's displayed text look trustworthy while the link itself leads to the phisher's site.
A third uses look-alike letters. The Cyrillic, Greek and Latin alphabets each have an o with the same shape but a different code point.
So an address can look identical and still be a different domain. It pays to read the whole address.

probes.question: True or false: look-alike letters from other alphabets can be used to fake a domain name.
